summary.intent: Start the planned parallel work lanes (A and B) from the NEXT-WORK plan, beginning with W2 SYS-RETRY (rerun after a tag is created but the push fails must finish the release). Along the way, the user required that the plan be kept local-only rather than in a PR.
summary.outcome: Closed PR #201 and moved the plan to a git-excluded local file. Implemented W2 SYS-RETRY in its own worktree with e2e tests, spec and architecture doc updates and a changeset; `just ci` passes (exit=0, 91.59% coverage) and the change is committed. The PR was not yet opened, and Lane A (W0/W1) was not started.

repo: Local tracking and handoff plans live in `.claude/plans/` (excluded via `.git/info/exclude`, not `.gitignore`) and must never be committed or put in a PR.
`just ci` must be run one at a time across worktrees; success must be judged by the log's own `exit=` line, not the background task's wrapper exit code.

Release tag selection previously treated an already-tagged version as settled. SYS-RETRY now derives a 'resumable' set, and the local plan observes releases already tagged at HEAD before deciding, so a failed push can be completed on rerun.

Several existing tests in `init.rs` (`preview_matches_release_dry_run_without_writing`) and `release/local.rs` relied on the old premise that a tagged version is settled, and had to be updated after the selection change.
The e2e release harness uses a fake publisher and fake git remote (`FAKE_GIT_REMOTE_TAGS`, `record_pushed_tag`, `CALLISTO_TEST_PUSH`) in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs`.
Changesets are added with the built binary into `.changeset/`; the W2 change used `.changeset/jolly-stags-roar.md`.
Release behavior is specified in `docs/specs/release.json` and `docs/architecture/release.md`, both updated for W2.

code.finding: Roster derivation now takes a 'resumable' set so releases tagged but not fully published are re-selected.
Added a helper that observes releases already tagged at HEAD, used by the local plan.
The local plan calls the tagged-at-HEAD observation before deciding; two tests here assumed tagged means settled and were revised.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first (tag created, push fails, rerun), then confirm it fails before implementing.
Run `just ci` in a background script and read the log's `exit=` line. The task-completion notification only reports that the wrapper exited.
Run tests without fail-fast to see all failures from a behavior change at once.
Prove behavior with the real tool or harness, not only fakes, as the user's feedback memory says.
Use the Edit tool instead of inline shell when the sandbox blocks inline `env` or git-mentioning scripts; macOS `sed` rejects some GNU-style one-liners.

friction: The plan file was not in the working branch; it existed only on PR #201's branch, which blocked starting work.
The assistant had put the local tracking plan into a PR (#201), which the user objected to; it had to be closed and moved.
The sandbox rejected inline `env` commands and inline scripts mentioning git, forcing script files and Edit-tool workarounds.
macOS `sed` rejected a one-liner for fixing imports.

The first lane summary gave a wrong plan file path.
